resources.name: Utah Crisis Line (Huntsman Mental Health Institute)
resources.description: Mental health crisis line
resources.servicesText:
Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year at no cost to you, our certified crisis workers provide:
compassionate and non-judgmental emotional support.
suicide prevention, information, and referrals.
follow-up services.
psycho-education about mental health issues.
education on how to support loved ones with mental health issues.
therapeutic assistance to individuals in emotional distress or psychiatric crisis.
coordination and dispatch response to individuals in the community as needed via the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team (MCOT) and/or first responders in coordination with other local mental health authorities.
The Utah Crisis Line collaborates with all 13 local mental health authorities across the state to ensure the best services are provided based on your location and needs. The goal of our services is to empower families and individuals with the tools and resources to receive the care that they need.

resources.name: Career Education
resources.description: Training and apprenticeship resources
resources.servicesText:
Path to Pro (pathtopro.com) 
Would you like training for a career in the trades? Home Depot offers a free, self-paced virtual training platform for learning a trade. Some of the career trades offered are drywall, paint, plumbing, electrical, welding, and others. 
Go to their website pathtopro.com and register online. 
Proxima Careers (proximacareers.org) 
Interested in a healthcare pathway? Proxima helps support and get you started in a Certified Nursing Assistant, Medical Assistant, Pharmacy Tech, or Emergency Medical Technician training program at no cost to you. 
Eligibility: 
Be 16+ years old 
Able to work in the USA 
Able to work 36+ hours after program completion at one of our employer partners 
Facing barriers to healthcare education 
See website (proximacareers.org) to sign up or for more information. Openings are limited. 
Provo City School District Adult Education 
Adult Basic Education: (801-374-4840) Adult classes designed to build basic skills in English and Math. 
Adult English Language Learning: (801-374-4904) If English is not a person's first language, the adult English classes provide English instruction. Call first as there is a wait list. Currently, the English classes are given at 750 West 200 North, Provo, until June 2026 when the building will be torn down. 
Alpine Adult Education (adulted.alpineschools.org) 
778 Bamberger Dr., American Fork, UT 84003 
801-610-8188 (for text only 385-269-0809) 
English Language Learners (ELL) for all levels: 
To register or get more information, call 801-227-8782. There is a $20 fee plus $10-30 book fees depending on the level. Nursery and/or preschool may be available to those who qualify. Classes in Orem (call 801-227-8782), Eagle Mountain (call 801-610-8897), or Saratoga Springs (call 801-901-0855) for more information or see their website adulted.alpineschools.org. 
Captain Your Story - My Story Matters 
Tools to change yourself and become the person you want to be. If you face: 
Fear of the unknown regarding your future. 
Guilt and self-blame for perceived failures. 
Frustration and helplessness in accessing appropriate resources and working with the system. 
Anxiety about the impact of employment on family dynamics and relationships. 
Stigma and judgement from social groups, adding to your isolation. 
Emotional exhaustion from constant worry and stress. 
Captain Your Story teaches core values and life skills. The practices and strategies are research-based. Learning is in person with an instructor, self-guided workbook. You will also be working with a mentor. 
For more information: 
801-477-7071 
Mystorymatters.org 
mailto:Office@mystorymatters.org 
Scholarships available. 
Project Read, Math, and Digital Skills (ProjectReadUtah.org) 
Project Read: Provides small group instruction as well as one-on-one tutoring to help individuals improve their ability to read and write, fill out job applications, create a budget, financial literacy and banking skills, health literacy, workforce prep, civics education. 
Project Math: Everyday math skills. 
Project Digital Skills: Essential computer and software skills, including Windows/Mac OS, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Google Docs, social media, career search skills, and technology in daily life. 
Qualifications: 
At least 16 years old. 
Have basic English skills. 
Read and write below a high school level. 
Provide proof of Utah residency. 
Commit to 6 instructional hours a week. 
Complete required testing. 
Pay associated program fees ($20/year and $20 for use of materials. The $20 materials fee is refundable at the end of the course if all materials are returned). 
Scholarships available. 
Submission form online. Call 801-448-7323 if you need help filling out. 
Project Read Office in Provo Library: 
550 North University Ave. Room #215, Provo, UT 84601 
801-448-7323 
Hours: Tuesday - Thursday 10 am - 7 pm. 
Friday 10 am - 4 pm. 
Mountainland Technical College (mtec.edu) 
Offering classes in: 
Healthcare (EMT, Dental Asst., Medical Asst., Pharmacy Tech, and more) 
Services (Cosmetology, Culinary Arts, Nail Tech and more) 
Trades (Automotive, Diesel, Welding, Commercial Driver's License, etc) 
Technology (Information Tech, Web Programming, etc.) 
Apprenticeships (Electrical, HVACR Tech, Plumbing) 
"Information Sessions" in person or virtual. Covers financial information, registration info, program details, scholarship info etc. Sign up on their website, opening page "View Session Dates". 
Campuses in Lehi, Orem, Provo, Spanish Fork, Payson. 
For more information, fill out the form online under "contact" or call 801-753-6282. Or register and attend an "Information Session" as mentioned above. 
Department of Workforce Services (jobs.utah.gov) 
If you are seeking an occupational license or professional certification DWFS may be able to help with the following resources: 
Paying for tuition, books, and required supplies. 
Paying required testing and licensing fees. 
Connecting with and paying for tutoring services, personalized coaching and financial support including applying for financial aid and navigating post-secondary education. 
Cash incentives for youth for completion of program. 
Apprenticeship opportunities: DWFS may be able to help find and research apprenticeship programs as well as provide funding for classroom training and required supplies. 
Completing a College Degree: Paying for tuition, books and required supplies as well as resources listed above. 
Paid internship opportunities to explore careers and gain workplace skills. Career assessment. 
How to apply: 
Go to jobs.utah.gov/career. Select the service or support you are interested in. 
Click "How to Apply" and then "Apply Now" to apply online. 
If you do not have a Utah ID account, you will need to create one. 
Or visit the nearest DWFS Employment Center. 
To receive funding you must meet eligibility requirements which vary based on program. 
Call 801-526-0950 (for all Utah County offices) for more information or go online to jobs.utah.gov. 
Offices open 8 am-5pm Monday-Friday in: 
1550 North 200 West (Provo 84604) 
1185 N. Canyon Creek Parkway (Spanish Fork 84660) 
557 West State St. (Lehi 84043

Location: 175 S. Freedom Blvd. Provo, UT 84601
Phone: 801-561-0881
Email: mailto:1432-br@peopleready.com
Type: Temporary employment agency for general labor, construction, hospitality, retail, manufacturing, warehouse/distribution, housekeeping/janitorial, disaster restoration, and more.
Features:
Build your own schedule.
Many jobs offer next-day pay.
Payment via direct deposit, check, or pay card.
Requirements:
Smartphone to download the “Jobstack” app (for applying and job notifications).
Two forms of ID (e.g., non-expired picture ID, Social Security card, jail release papers, birth certificate).
May need steel toe shoes and long pants for most jobs.
---

Type: On-demand work—pick up shifts when you want using the “Baconwork OnDemand” app.
Features:
View shift details (company, time, pay, type of work).
Flexible, temporary work (event staffing, catering, warehouse, general labor, etc.).
No specific skill required—just willingness to work hard.
You control your schedule.
After each shift, you’re rated (1–5 stars); payment follows rating.

Download the app and create a work profile.
Browse and apply for positions based on your interests and experience.
Accept shifts that suit you.
Earnings are transferred automatically after timesheet approval.

Search jobs easily.
Target jobs by area and keywords.
Add jobs to favorites or remove those you’re not interested in.

Choose services (pet boarding, house sitting, dog walking, drop-in visits, doggy daycare, dog training).
Set rates, availability, and pet preferences.
Create your profile (experience, etc.).

resources.name: Maternity resources
resources.description: Financial assistance and prenatal care
resources.servicesText:
---
**Resources for Women who are Pregnant**
---
**Emergency Medicaid** (For Delivery Costs)
Utah offers Emergency Medicaid for non-citizens (including undocumented immigrants) who meet income requirements.
Coverage: This covers labor and delivery charges for the mother.
Eligibility: Must be a Utah resident, have low/zero income, and meet the financial criteria for regular Medicaid.
Application: The mother can apply one month before the expected delivery date.
Baby's Coverage: An infant born to a mother on Emergency Medicaid is eligible for full Medicaid for their first year.
---
**Hospital Charity Care & Financial Assistance**
---
**Non-profit hospitals in Utah (such as Intermountain Health and CommonSpirit Health (Holy** ** Cross Health) are legally required to have financial assistance policies.**
Utah Valley Hospital in Provo, American Fork Hospital, Orem Community Hospital, and Holy Cross Hospital- Mountain Point in Lehi are non-profit hospitals.
Action: Contact the hospital's billing department immediately to apply for "charity care" or "financial assistance".
Eligibility: Generally based on income. Families with zero income likely qualify for 100% forgiveness of the bill.
Process: They will need to fill out an application, likely providing a letter explaining their current financial status.
Uninsured Discount: If they do not qualify for Medicaid, hospitals often offer automatic discounts for uninsured patients.
---
**"Baby Your Baby"** (For Prenatal Care)
Baby Your Baby (BYB) is a Utah program that provides temporary Medicaid for low-income pregnant women.
While BYB primarily covers outpatient prenatal care, the application process acts as a bridge to other, more comprehensive coverage.
Action: Call the Baby Your Baby hotline at 1-800-826-9662.

resources.name: Phone and internet service
resources.description: Low-cost phone and internet providers
resources.servicesText:
---
**Phone and Internet Service**
---
**Lifeline Phone and Internet Service**
A Federal program that provides discounted telephone service or discounted internet service through contracted service providers to low-income individuals and families.
Lifeline pays up to $9.25 towards a monthly phone, internet, or bundled service bill, or up to $34.25 per month for Tribal households.
You may be eligible to get Lifeline if:
Your income is 135% or less of the federal poverty guidelines, or
You participate in a government assistance program such as SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal public housing assistance, National School Lunch Program, or a Tribal specific program.
How to sign up:
Sign up at https://www.lifelinesupport.org.
After you qualify, choose a phone or internet company near you and sign up for service with them.
You can also sign up via mail (see lifelinesupport.org), or with a participating wireless provider.
---
**Phone companies working with Lifeline:**
(Some offer free service, free phones, or low-cost plans. Check online first to see if you are eligible or do the qualification process directly with one of the wireless companies.)
* Airtalk Wireless (https://airtalkwireless.com/my-state/Utah)
* Assurance Wireless (https://assurancewireless.com) 1-888-321-5880
* Tru Connect (https://truconnect.com) 1-800-430-0443
* EnTouch Wireless (https://apply4lifeline.Entouchwireless.com) 1-888-594-0579
* Life Wireless (https://lifewireless.com) 1-888-543-3620
* Safelink Wireless (https://safelinkwireless.com)
* Stand Up Wireless (https://standupwireless.com) 1-800-234-9473
---
**Low-cost Internet Providers**
As low as $15/month. Based on Lifeline eligibility rules (see above). Check for availability in your area online. Applications online.
* Xfinity "Internet Essentials" (https://xfinity.com/learn/internet-service/internet-essentials)
* AT&T "Access" (https://att.com/access)
* Spectrum "Internet Assist" (https://spectrum.com/internet/spectrum-internet-assist)
* T-Mobile: "Project 10 Million" – Free Internet Access for eligible K-12 Students
Benefits: Free mobile hotspot and Free 200GB of internet per year for 5 years.
Eligibility: K-12 students enrolled in one of the following: SNAP, Medicaid, National School Lunch Program, or Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservation.
To apply: Visit https://t-mobile.com/brand/project-10-million
Must have proof of participation in one of the government programs listed above.

4. Viva en el campus y únase a un grupo estudiantil
5. Conéctese con empleadores después de graduarse

Job Corps tiene política de ***tolerancia cero** para drogas, alcohol y violencia. El proceso de solicitud requiere documentación y puede llevar tiempo.
---
**¿Quiénes pueden asistir?**
Debe:
* Cumplir requisitos de bajos ingresos
* Tener entre 16 y 24 años
* Ser ciudadano, residente legal o autorizado para trabajar
* Estar dispuesto a mejorar su educación y habilidades

Incluye testimonio de estudiante (Tivia).
---
**Capacitación práctica en 10 industrias**
* Manufactura avanzada
* Reparación de automóviles y maquinaria
* Construcción
* Finanzas y negocios
* Atención médica
* Seguridad nacional
* Hotelería
* Tecnologías de la información
* Recursos renovables
* Transporte

Más de 100 programas disponibles.
Pre‑apprenticeships también disponibles.
---
**Capacitación avanzada**
Job Corps ofrece programas avanzados en centros seleccionados, incluyendo:
* Clearfield (Utah)
* Earle C. Clements (Kentucky)
Instructores ayudan a explorar opciones y requisitos.
---
**Vida en el recinto universitario**
Incluye:
* 3 comidas al día
* Atención médica
* Materiales de capacitación
* Clubes y liderazgo
* Apoyo comunitario

Ofrecen opciones no residenciales.
**Explorar centros:** jobcorps.gov/explore
**YouTube:** youtube.com/doljobcorps

**Y2Y Youth 2 Youth Campaign**
Enfoque en violencia, drogas y salud mental.
---
**Su fórmula para el éxito**
1. Acomódese
2. Comience a aprender
3. Capacitación práctica
4. Prepárese para el éxito
5. Graduación
---
**¿Qué pasa después de Job Corps?**
Recibirá apoyo en:
* Búsqueda laboral
* Vivienda y transporte
* Currículum
* Habilidades de entrevista

Job Corps conecta con empleadores y capacita para industrias que están contratando.
Incluye testimonio de Kasandra.
---
**No existe mejor momento para centrarse en su futuro**
Más de 120 centros en EE. UU. y Puerto Rico.
El consejero de admisiones ayuda a completar la solicitud y elegir centro.
Incluye mapa nacional de centros Job Corps.
---
**Información final**
Job Corps es un programa del Departamento de Trabajo de EE. UU.
